Question: Acute-angled triangle \(ABC\) is inscribed in a circle with center at \(O;\) \(\overset{\frown}{AB}=120^\circ\) and \(\overset{\frown}{BC}=72^\circ.\) A point \(E\) is taken in minor arc \(AC\) such that \(OE\) is perpendicular to \(AC.\) Then the ratio of the magnitudes of angles \(OBE\) and \(BAC\) is:
Solution:
The acute-angle condition determines which arcs to use. By the inscribed-angle theorem, each arc between two vertices that does not contain the third vertex measures twice an acute angle, so it is less than \(180^\circ\). Thus the given \(120^\circ\) and \(72^\circ\) arcs are consecutive arcs of the triangle. The remaining arc \(AC\), which does not contain \(B\), measures
\[
360^\circ-120^\circ-72^\circ=168^\circ.
\]
It is therefore the minor arc \(AC\).

A diameter perpendicular to a chord bisects its minor arc. Since \(OE\perp AC\) and \(E\) lies on minor arc \(AC\), we obtain
\[
\widehat{AE}=\widehat{EC}=84^\circ.
\]
The arc from \(B\) through \(C\) to \(E\) measures \(72^\circ+84^\circ=156^\circ\). This is less than \(180^\circ\), so \(\angle BOE=156^\circ\). Because \(OB=OE\) are radii, triangle \(OBE\) is isosceles, giving
\[
\angle OBE=\frac{180^\circ-156^\circ}{2}=12^\circ.
\]
Also, \(\angle BAC\) intercepts the \(72^\circ\) arc \(BC\), so it equals \(36^\circ\). Hence the required ratio is
\[
\frac{\angle OBE}{\angle BAC}
=\frac{12}{36}=\boxed{\frac13},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
